keyTakeaways: Here are 12 original Diwali sher for friends, two each for six kinds of friend, every line 8 to 12 words, in Devanagari, Roman and English.
Platts' 1884 dictionary separates the words: dost is 'a friend, one beloved', jigri 'belonging to the liver or heart', langotiya 'an old friend (from childhood)'.

faqs.question: What is the difference between dost and yaar in a Diwali message?
faqs.answer: Both mean friend, but they set different tones. Platts' 1884 dictionary gives dost as 'a friend, one beloved' and yaar as 'a friend … companion, comrade', and in practice yaar is the more casual of the two. Use yaar or tu for a friend you joke with, and dost or tum for a newer or more formal friendship.

faqs.question: What does jigri dost literally mean?
faqs.answer: Jigri comes from jigar, the liver, which older Urdu treats as a seat of feeling the way English uses the heart. Platts (1884, p. 384) defines jigri as 'belonging to the liver or heart' and then 'dear, beloved, intimate, close (friend)'. A jigri dost is the friend closest to you.

faqs.question: Why is a childhood friend called a langotiya yaar?
faqs.answer: Langoti is a loincloth, the simplest garment a small child wears. Platts (1884, p. 966) records langotiya as 'a playmate; an old friend (from childhood); a very intimate friend', so a langotiya yaar is someone who has known you since before you wore proper clothes.

faqs.question: Can I send these shayari to a female friend?
faqs.answer: Yes. Most of the 12 sher use tu or tum, which carry no gender, and the verbs written in the first person can be switched to the feminine form (kehti hoon, karti hoon) without breaking the rhyme. In the laddoo sher, change ladka to ladki.

faqs.question: Are these Diwali shayari copied from another site?
faqs.answer: No. All 12 were written for this page and checked word by word against the lines in our earlier Diwali posts so that none repeats. You can send them without credit, and changing a word or a name to fit your friend is encouraged.

faqs.question: What day should I send Diwali wishes to friends in 2027?
faqs.answer: Lakshmi Puja, the main day of Diwali, falls on Friday 29 October 2027, with Dhanteras on Wednesday 27 October and Choti Diwali on Thursday 28 October. Send group plans on Dhanteras, a childhood friend's sher on Choti Diwali and your closest friend's after the evening aarti on the 29th.

faqs.question: Is a funny or an emotional shayari better for a best friend?
faqs.answer: Pick the one that makes them laugh at a shared memory. In Robin Dunbar's 2017 survey of 2,000 UK adults, laughter and reminiscing at meals had the strongest effects on feeling closer, while jokes alone had no significant effect. That study was about meals, not messages, so this is our inference.

faqs.question: What should I send a friend who is grieving during Diwali?
faqs.answer: Send plain words rather than verse: two sentences that name the person they lost and offer your company. If they welcome something gentler, the hard-year sher above offers to light their share of the diyas and to sit quietly instead of celebrating.

faqs.question: Can I put my own shayari inside the SubhSandesh Diwali card for a friend?
faqs.answer: Yes. Choose the friend mode on the Happy Diwali template and write your sher into the letter sealed in the shagun liffafa, or into the wish on each diya. You can add up to six photos to the sky lanterns, and the private link opens in any browser with no app or account.

faqs.question: Should I write the shayari in Hindi script or in Roman letters?
faqs.answer: Send it in the script your friend reads fastest. Many friends type Hindi in Roman letters on WhatsApp, so the Roman version given under each sher reads naturally in a chat, while the Devanagari version looks better on a card or an image.

article.contentMarkdown:
# Diwali Shayari for Friends: 12 Original Dosti Sher, Sorted by the Kind of Friend

Diwali shayari for friends works best when it names the kind of friend: the langotiya yaar, the jigri dost, the group chat, a new friend, the friend whose family is yours, and the friend in a hard year. Below are 12 original sher, two for each, in Devanagari with Roman and an English gloss, written for this page, not collected. Send them on Friday, 29 October 2027, Lakshmi Puja evening.

Keep each one to two lines. On SubhSandesh, 48.3% of the 57,456 recorded views of shared pages were on a phone (measured 24 September 2026), so the sher has to land on one small screen. People also write these late: on Raksha Bandhan 2026, our nearest festival analogue (n = 89 pages, not Diwali data), 49.4% of pages were built on the festival day itself.

## Dost, yaar, jigri, langotiya: four words Platts (1884) keeps apart

Each Hindi-Urdu word for a friend sets a tone. John T. Platts' *A Dictionary of Urdu, Classical Hindi, and English* (1884) defines [dost as "a friend, one beloved"](https://dsal.uchicago.edu/cgi-bin/app/platts_query.py?qs=%D8%AF%D9%88%D8%B3%D8%AA&searchhws=yes) on page 534, and records the idiom *dostī kā dam bharnā*, "to make a boast of friendship", or to pretend it.

[Yār, on page 1247](https://dsal.uchicago.edu/cgi-bin/app/platts_query.py?qs=%DB%8C%D8%A7%D8%B1&searchhws=yes), is looser: "a friend", also "companion, comrade". Its idioms range from *yār-ě-ghār*, "a companion in a cave", to *yār-mār*, "one who betrays his friend".

The closest two words are older images. [Jigrī, on page 384](https://dsal.uchicago.edu/cgi-bin/app/platts_query.py?qs=%D8%AC%DA%AF%D8%B1%DB%8C&searchhws=yes), means "belonging to the liver or heart", then "intimate, close (friend)". [Laṅgoṭiyā, on page 966](https://dsal.uchicago.edu/cgi-bin/app/platts_query.py?qs=%E0%A4%B2%E0%A4%82%E0%A4%97%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%9F%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE&searchhws=yes), comes from *laṅgoṭī*, a loincloth, and means "an old friend (from childhood)".

## 12 original Diwali shayari for friends, by kind of friend

Each line runs 8 to 12 words. Copy both lines together; "ladka" can become "ladki" without breaking the rhyme.

### 1. Langotiya yaar: the friend from your shorts-wearing days

Use *tu*. This friend has seen every Diwali of yours, so the sher can be cheeky.

> नेकर वाले दिनों से जो मेरा हाथ थामे चल रहा है,\
> वो यार हर दिवाली मेरे घर का दीया बनकर जल रहा है।\
> *Nekar vaale dinon se jo mera haath thaame chal raha hai, vo yaar har Diwali mere ghar ka diya bankar jal raha hai.*\
> The friend holding my hand since our days in shorts burns each Diwali as my home's lamp.

> माँ अब भी पूछती है, "वो दुबला-सा लड़का कब आएगा?"\
> अब तोंद है, दाढ़ी है, पर पहला लड्डू तो वही खाएगा।\
> *Maa ab bhi poochhti hai, "vo dubla-sa ladka kab aayega?" Ab tond hai, daadhi hai, par pehla laddoo to vahi khaayega.*\
> Ma still asks when that skinny boy is coming; paunch and beard now, but the first laddoo is still his.

### 2. Jigri dost: the one person you write to properly

Drop the jokes here. Say the thing once.

> जिगर का टुकड़ा यूँ ही नहीं, तुझे जिगरी कहता हूँ,\
> दीयों की हर लौ में तेरे होने का शुक्र करता हूँ।\
> *Jigar ka tukda yoon hi nahin, tujhe jigri kehta hoon, diyon ki har lau mein tere hone ka shukr karta hoon.*\
> I don't call you jigri, a piece of my heart, for nothing; in every diya's flame I give thanks for you.

> सारी दुनिया को "हैप्पी दिवाली" फ़ॉरवर्ड कर दिया,\
> तुझे लिखने बैठा तो आधा घंटा सोच में बीत गया।\
> *Saari duniya ko "Happy Diwali" forward kar diya, tujhe likhne baitha to aadha ghanta soch mein beet gaya.*\
> I forwarded "Happy Diwali" to the world; writing to you took half an hour of thinking.

### 3. Yaaron ki toli: the group chat that never makes a plan

Post these in the chat, not one-to-one. The point is that everyone laughs at once.

> ग्रुप में सौ मैसेज, फिर भी किसी ने प्लान नहीं बनाया,\
> हर बार की तरह इस बार भी "चलो देखते हैं" ही आया।\
> *Group mein sau message, phir bhi kisi ne plan nahin banaaya, har baar ki tarah is baar bhi "chalo dekhte hain" hi aaya.*\
> A hundred messages, no plan; as always, just "let's see".

> आधी रात, नुक्कड़ की टपरी, और पाँच यारों की चाय,\
> इतनी रौशन महफ़िल कोई महल भी दिखाए तो दिखाए।\
> *Aadhi raat, nukkad ki tapri, aur paanch yaaron ki chai, itni raushan mehfil koi mahal bhi dikhaaye to dikhaaye.*\
> Midnight, the corner tea stall, five friends' chai: let any palace show a brighter gathering, if it can.

### 4. Naya dost: a friend you made this year

A first Diwali as friends deserves marking. Use *tum* if you are still finding your register.

> साल भर पहले तक तू बस एक अनजाना नाम था,\
> आज मेरी दिवाली की लिस्ट में तेरा पहला मक़ाम था।\
> *Saal bhar pehle tak tu bas ek anjaana naam tha, aaj meri Diwali ki list mein tera pehla maqaam tha.*\
> A year ago you were a stranger's name; today, first on my Diwali list.

> नई दोस्ती है, अभी सारे क़िस्से बाक़ी हैं,\
> ये पहली दिवाली है, अभी सौ दिवालियाँ बाक़ी हैं।\
> *Nayi dosti hai, abhi saare qisse baaqi hain, ye pehli Diwali hai, abhi sau Diwaliyaan baaqi hain.*\
> A new friendship, all its stories still to come; this is our first Diwali, and a hundred remain.

### 5. The friend whose family became yours

Some friends come with a second mother and kitchen. These thank the whole house.

> तेरी माँ की पूजा की थाली में मेरा भी नाम आता है,\
> दोस्ती का रिश्ता, देख, कहाँ तक घर बनाता है।\
> *Teri maa ki pooja ki thaali mein mera bhi naam aata hai, dosti ka rishta, dekh, kahaan tak ghar banaata hai.*\
> My name comes up at your mother's puja thali too; see how far friendship goes in making a home.

> तेरे घर की एक चाबी बरसों से मेरे गुच्छे में है,\
> दिवाली हो या कोई दिन, मेरा दीया तेरे कमरे में है।\
> *Tere ghar ki ek chaabi barson se mere guchchhe mein hai, Diwali ho ya koi din, mera diya tere kamre mein hai.*\
> A key to your house has sat on my keyring for years; Diwali or any day, my lamp is in your room.

### 6. A friend having a hard year

Loss or illness can make a bright festival feel loud. These offer company, not cheer.

> इस साल तेरी झोली में अँधेरा कुछ ज़्यादा आया,\
> तो सुन, इस बार मैंने तेरे हिस्से का दीया भी जलाया।\
> *Is saal teri jholi mein andhera kuchh zyaada aaya, to sun, is baar maine tere hisse ka diya bhi jalaaya.*\
> This year more dark fell into your lap; so listen, this time I lit your share of the diyas too.

> तू कहे तो रौनक़ नहीं, बस चुपचाप साथ बैठेंगे,\
> रौशनी की रात भी हम तेरी रफ़्तार से चलेंगे।\
> *Tu kahe to raunaq nahin, bas chupchaap saath baithenge, raushni ki raat bhi hum teri raftaar se chalenge.*\
> Say the word and we skip the fuss and just sit together; even on this night of lights, we go at your pace.

## Why a shared memory beats a joke: Dunbar's 2,000-adult survey (2017)

A joke is the easy friend sher, but Robin Dunbar's 2017 paper in *Adaptive Human Behavior and Physiology* suggests the joke is not what bonds. In a [UK survey of 2,000 adults](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC6979515), laughter (at 67.9% of reported evening meals) and reminiscing (51.5%) had the strongest effects on feeling closer to dinner companions, while jokes alone had no significant effect (p = 0.174).

Dunbar concludes that "it seems to be the laughter itself, whatever it is triggered by, that creates the sense of bonding". The study covered British meals, not festival messages, so applying it here is our inference: pick a sher that makes a friend laugh at a shared memory.

Chung and colleagues, in [*Royal Society Open Science* (2024)](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC11521598), studied 112 strangers watching emotional videos in pairs. Intense emotion was linked to reciprocal prosocial attitudes, an effect that depended on joint attention to the same screen.

## Which sher for which friend: a 5-row comparison

The 2027 days are verified dates. The timings are our suggestions, not a muhurat.

| Kind of friend | Word (Platts page) | Pronoun | Sher above | When to send in 2027 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Childhood friend | langotiya yaar (p. 966) | tu | 1, the laddoo sher | Thu 28 Oct, Choti Diwali |
| Closest friend | jigri dost (p. 384) | tu or tum | 2, the half-hour sher | Fri 29 Oct, after the aarti |
| Group chat | yaar, plural yaaron (p. 1247) | tum log | 3, the "let's see" sher | Wed 27 Oct, Dhanteras |
| New friend | dost (p. 534) | tum | 4, the hundred Diwalis sher | Fri 29 Oct, early evening |
| Friend in a hard year | dost or yaar | tu | 6, the share-of-the-diyas sher | Fri 29 Oct, privately |

## Sending it on 29 October 2027: group chat, one-to-one or a page

Group sher belong in the group, where everyone reads them at once, the joint-attention point from 2024. Jigri and hard-year sher belong one-to-one, ideally as a voice note, which nobody mistakes for a forward.

To make the sher something your friend opens, [SubhSandesh's interactive Diwali card](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-diwali) has a friend mode that changes the default wishes, blessing and reply. Put the sher in the letter inside the red-and-gold shagun liffafa and add up to six old photos to the sky lanterns; it takes about 5 minutes and opens in any browser.

Across the platform a shared page is viewed 11.1 times on average (measured 24 September 2026), so a sher placed there tends to be reread. For a langotiya yaar with a phone full of old photos, the [photo jigsaw where each piece reveals a line of your letter](https://subhsandesh.in/photo-puzzle) is the other fit, but it is not a Diwali template.

## When a shayari is the wrong Diwali message for a friend: 3 cases

Three situations call for plain words instead. A friend grieving someone this year may not want rhyme; two sentences naming the person they lost are kinder.

A friend you drifted from will read a polished couplet as a forward, so ask one plain question about their year. A friendly colleague is better served by a short English wish; *jigri* from a manager reads oddly.

SubhSandesh is also the wrong tool for a group of ten friends. The Diwali card is built for one person, with two names and one letter, so post the group sher in the chat.

serp.note: Every top-10 page is a numbered shayari list; none sorts friends by kind, explains dost/yaar/jigri/langotiya, gives an English gloss, or is dated for Diwali 2027. Top 5 fetched in full (HTML, word counts ~2,300–2,900 incl. chrome). Cannibalisation gate: closest existing post is b1 diwali-shayari (batchMeta.serp measured 2026-10-22 via Firecrawl India); shared URLs with this SERP = 0 of 10 (below the 4-URL threshold). Angle sharpened anyway: friend-only, sorted by kind of friend, Platts entries not used by any Diwali post (b1 used shi'r/radif, b2 2-line misra/qafiya, miss-you firaq/judai/yaad).

structuralLimitations: SERP is DuckDuckGo HTML (kl=in-en), lower confidence than a Google India SERP; WebSearch is US-indexed and returned spam, so it was not used. Search budget: 2 of 3 used (1 WebSearch, 1 DuckDuckGo).

No Diwali usage data exists; first-party lines are platform-wide (phone-open share, views per page) and the Raksha Bandhan 2026 analogue (n = 89), labelled as such in the body. Per the brief, 'first-party data' means facts.md only; our own SERP and n-gram measurements are not counted toward it.

Dunbar (2017) measured UK shared meals and Chung et al. (2024) measured strangers watching videos in a lab; applying either to Diwali messages between Indian friends is labelled in the body as our inference.

Line originality: every Devanagari line was 4-word n-gram matched against all Devanagari text in 81 existing Diwali posts (b1, b2 on disk, 2026-08-19, diwali-gift-for-wife) and every Roman line 5-gram matched against their bodies; two hits on common phrases ('दिवाली की रात भी', 'har diye ki lau mein') were rewritten. auditReport.honestAssessment: The measured top 10 is ten interchangeable Hindi shayari lists; this is the only page that sorts original friend sher by kind of friend, explains the four friend words from a citable 1884 dictionary, glosses every line in English, and uses a peer-reviewed finding to say which sher to pick. It sits on a low-authority domain against long-indexed shayari sites, its SERP was measured on DuckDuckGo rather than Google India, and its first-party data is platform-wide rather than Diwali-specific, so expect months, not weeks.
